knowledge_point.title: Simplifying Expressions in Radians Using the Sum and Difference Formulas

question.:question/problem: Express $\cos\left(x-\frac{5\pi}{3}\right)$ in terms of $\sin x$ and $\cos x$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the difference formula:

$$
\cos(u-v)=\cos u\cos v+\sin u\sin v
$$

With $u=x$ and $v=\frac{5\pi}{3}$, the exact values are $\cos\left(\frac{5\pi}{3}\right)=\frac{1}{2}$ and $\sin\left(\frac{5\pi}{3}\right)=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$. Substitute and collect the terms in the requested order:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\cos\left(x-\frac{5\pi}{3}\right)&=\cos x\cos\left(\frac{5\pi}{3}\right)+\sin x\sin\left(\frac{5\pi}{3}\right)\\
&=\cos x\cdot\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+\sin x\cdot\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\\
&=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin x+\frac{1}{2}\cos x.
\end{aligned}
$$

error_profile.mistake: wrong quadrant signs for both values
